interactions.label: A bone marrow aspirate shows 15% blast cells. Cytogenetic analysis reveals a t(8

params.question: A bone marrow aspirate shows 15% blast cells. Cytogenetic analysis reveals a t(8;21) translocation. How should this case be classified?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MDS is a distinct entity with its own diagnostic criteria. While blasts are below the usual 20% threshold, certain cytogenetic abnormalities override the blast count for diagnosing acute myeloid leukaemia.

answers.text: Acute myeloid leukaemia, because t(8;21) is a defining cytogenetic abnormality

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The WHO classification recognises t(8;21), t(15;17), and inv(16) as defining abnormalities that diagnose AML regardless of blast percentage — these are the chromosomal exceptions to the 20% rule.

answers.text: Chronic myeloid leukaemia, because blasts are below 20%

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CML is defined by the BCR-ABL1 fusion from t(9;22), not t(8;21). A blast count below 20% alone does not make a leukaemia chronic — the specific cytogenetic abnormality and maturation pattern matter.

answers.text: Cannot be classified as acute leukaemia until blasts reach 20%

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The 20% threshold is the general WHO rule, but t(8;21), t(15;17), and inv(16) are explicit exceptions — they define AML even when blasts fall below 20%.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the chromosomal exceptions: t(8;21), t(15;17), and inv(16) diagnose AML even when blasts fall below the 20% WHO threshold.
Well done. Certain chromosomal translocations define AML regardless of blast count — a critical exception to the 20% WHO threshold.

interactions.label: According to the two-hit model proposed by Gilliland and Griffin, a single class

params.question: According to the two-hit model proposed by Gilliland and Griffin, a single class of mutation — either proliferative (Class I) or differentiation-blocking (Class II) — is sufficient to produce the full acute leukaemia phenotype.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. The two-hit model requires cooperation between both classes: Class I mutations drive proliferation, and Class II mutations block differentiation. Neither alone is sufficient — together, they produce the leukaemic phenotype and explain why specific cytogenetic lesions predict prognosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Class I mutations (e.g. FLT3-ITD, RAS) drive proliferation and survival, while Class II mutations (e.g. RUNX1 fusion, PML-RARα) block differentiation. Neither class alone causes leukaemia; both must cooperate.

interactions.label: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia (FAB M3) carries a high risk of disseminated intra

params.question: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia (FAB M3) carries a high risk of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Which chromosomal abnormality produces the fusion protein responsible for both the maturation block and this coagulation complication?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: t(9;22) creates the Philadelphia chromosome, seen in chronic myeloid leukaemia and some cases of ALL. It is not associated with APL or DIC.
inv(16) is associated with the myelomonocytic AML subtype with abnormal eosinophils. It carries a favourable prognosis but is not linked to APL or DIC.
t(8;21) is associated with FAB M2 (AML with maturation) and Auer rods. It carries a favourable prognosis but is not the translocation behind APL.

Correct. The PML-RARα fusion blocks myeloid maturation at the promyelocyte stage. These abnormal promyelocytes release tissue factor, triggering DIC. All-trans retinoic acid overcomes this differentiation block, making APL the most curable AML subtype.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key association: t(15;17) → PML-RARα fusion → maturation arrest at promyelocyte stage → tissue factor release → DIC. Treatment is all-trans retinoic acid combined with arsenic trioxide.
Excellent. APL with t(15;17) is the most curable form of AML when treated with ATRA and arsenic trioxide, but DIC at presentation makes it a medical emergency requiring urgent recognition.

interactions.label: A bone marrow aspirate shows 40% blasts. Myeloperoxidase and Sudan Black B stain

params.question: A bone marrow aspirate shows 40% blasts. Myeloperoxidase and Sudan Black B stains are both negative. Which additional finding would most strongly support a diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia over acute myeloid leukaemia?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CD34 is a haematopoietic stem cell marker expressed in both AML and ALL. It cannot distinguish between the two lineages on its own.
Non-specific esterase is positive in the monocytic subtypes of AML (M4 and M5). Its positivity would actually favour an AML diagnosis, not ALL.

Correct. TdT is the single clearest lymphoid lineage marker — it is positive in both B-ALL and T-ALL but negative in most AML. Combined with negative MPO and Sudan Black B, TdT positivity strongly supports ALL.

answers.text: Coarse magenta blocks on periodic acid-Schiff stain alone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PAS positivity with coarse blocks suggests B-ALL, but PAS is less specific than TdT. TdT covers both B-ALL and T-ALL, making it the more reliable single marker for confirming lymphoid lineage.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the diagnostic hierarchy: MPO and Sudan Black B identify myeloid lineage; TdT is the key lymphoid marker (positive in both B-ALL and T-ALL, negative in most AML). CD34 appears in both and cannot distinguish them.

Well done. The diagnostic algorithm: negative MPO and Sudan Black B exclude myeloid lineage; positive TdT confirms lymphoid lineage. Flow cytometry then separates B-ALL (CD19, CD10) from T-ALL (CD3, CD7).

interactions.label: In tumour lysis syndrome, uric acid crystal deposition in the renal tubules can

params.question: In tumour lysis syndrome, uric acid crystal deposition in the renal tubules can cause acute kidney injury. Which drug acts by directly converting existing uric acid into the soluble metabolite allantoin?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rasburicase is a recombinant uricase enzyme that directly converts existing uric acid to allantoin, a water-soluble compound easily excreted by the kidneys. It acts rapidly, making it preferred when uric acid levels are already dangerously high.
Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, blocking new uric acid production. However, it does not break down uric acid that has already formed, so it acts more slowly in an acute crisis.

Hydration increases renal flow and dilutes uric acid concentration, but it does not convert uric acid to allantoin. It is an essential supportive measure used alongside specific uric acid-lowering therapy.
Calcium gluconate addresses the hypocalcaemia of TLS (caused by reciprocal calcium drop from hyperphosphataemia) but has no effect on uric acid levels or renal tubular crystal deposition.

overallFeedback.feedback: The mechanism-based distinction: allopurinol blocks uric acid production by inhibiting xanthine oxidase, while rasburicase is a recombinant uricase that directly converts existing uric acid to allantoin. In an acute TLS crisis, rasburicase acts faster.
Exactly right. Rasburicase enzymatically degrades existing uric acid to allantoin, providing rapid clearance. Allopurinol prevents further production but cannot remove what has already accumulated.
